title: Scale Identification Skill
purpose: Given a set of notes (or a song's pitch-class histogram), determine the scale/key/mode and its Hindustani thaat equivalent.
method: 1. Identify the TONIC (root / Sa) first — the note the melody most often returns to and rests on. In Hindustani music this is Sa.
2. Normalize every observed note to a pitch class (C, C#, D, ... ignoring octave).
3. Sort the unique pitch classes relative to the tonic and read the interval pattern (in semitones from Sa).
4. Match that interval pattern against known scale formulas to name the scale/mode.
5. Convert to the Hindustani thaat using the thaat table below.
pitfalls: The tonic is NOT always the most frequent note — it is the note where phrases RESOLVE and rest.
Relative keys share the same pitch classes (e.g. F# Major and D# Natural Minor both have F# G# A# B C# D# E#). Use where the melody rests to pick the true tonic.
A song may use notes outside the strict scale as passing tones — do not overfit to a single out-of-scale note.
